0.content:
Crepus Ragnvindr, the former master of the Dawn Winery, was Diluc's father. He had wanted to be a knight and failed to qualify, and he never received a Vision, so he hoped his son would become the most esteemed knight of all and taught him that the world would never turn its back on the faithful. On Diluc's eighteenth birthday (after a coming-of-age celebration at Angel's Share, in the manga), a monster attacked the transport fleet carrying father and son. Crepus repelled it with an "unknown evil power", a Delusion, which then backfired and mortally wounded him. In Diluc's account Crepus died in his son's arms. He also took in Kaeya and raised him as a son. Crepus's employees, Elzer among them, mourned him.

Kaeya's Vision story gives a harsher account: Diluc ended his father's life to free him from unbearable agony. Diluc has never confirmed or denied it. Diluc still quotes Crepus's sayings, such as "Sometimes, life can change in an instant." Varka says Crepus, Varka and Eroch were once three young friends who dreamed of the future together: a rich young master who wanted to be a knight but inherited the winery, a hot-headed rule-breaker who became Grand Master, and a third who got neither the wealth nor the power he wanted.

1.content:
Kaeya Alberich is Crepus's adopted son and the current Cavalry Captain, the post Diluc once held. As young men they were Mondstadt's most eye-catching pair, almost like twins, protecting the city "in both light and dark". When Crepus died, Kaeya arrived too late, and in shock he smirked that the world was "truly... fascinating". That night, consumed by guilt, Kaeya told Diluc the truth: he was an agent of Khaenri'ah left in Mondstadt by his birth father. The brothers fought, and Kaeya's Cryo Vision awoke in the clash. It has been a long time since Kaeya called Diluc "brother".

Today they needle each other: Diluc says Kaeya can be trusted halfway at best, and Kaeya says Diluc was cute as a lad but is now no fun. They still work together. Kaeya knows Diluc is the Darknight Hero, set Huffman to watch him as a test, and then declined to expose him: "it isn't his style". Adelinde wonders when they will finally settle their issues. In the 6.4 letter scene Kaeya teases Diluc that he used to be constantly at odds with the Knights.

2.content:
After his return, an unknown guardian began working at night. Monsters were found dead in the wilds, wanted thieves turned up hanging bound in the statue plaza, and an Abyss Mage the Knights hunted was found already dead. A smell of burning and a flash of red flame were all anyone saw. Tavern talk named him the "Darknight Hero". Diluc publicly scorns the name. Elzer is one of the few who know. In his Story Quest (1.0) the Traveler caught him killing an Abyss Mage. When the Abyss Order sent a challenge, he interrogated a mage named Landrich for the attack plan, lured a slime horde with experimental bait as a diversion, shamed the watching knight Huffman into leaving his post, wiped out the horde and was back behind the bar with his "patrons" (winery staff) as his alibi. Kaeya saw through it and kept quiet.

Paimon nicknamed him "Captain Pyro". In 6.6, when Paimon asked whether the Darknight Hero had cleaned up some monsters, he said the traces did not match "his" style, still pretending not to know him.

3.comment: Diluc: Dawn Winery and Angel's Share
3.content:
The Dawn Winery is Mondstadt's chief winery, owned by the Ragnvindr Clan for about a thousand years. It is famous for Dandelion Wine. It controls roughly half of Mondstadt's wine trade and owns Angel's Share, the city's best-known tavern and centre of information, where Charles tends bar and Diluc sometimes takes over. The motto on its plaque is "Shine True". Diluc introduced alcohol-free drinks such as apple cider and keeps grape juice stocked.

The household: Elzer, who served Crepus and regarded him as a father figure, runs much of the business and chairs the Mondstadt Wine Guild, and he handles reimbursements. Adelinde, the head housemaid, ran the winery while Diluc was abroad; she knew both boys as children and still tells stories of their mischief. Angel's Share does not run tabs. The winery's caravans pass through Dornman Port, and its products are counterfeited abroad.

4.comment: Diluc: The Knights of Favonius and Eroch
4.content:
Diluc passed the Knights' trials and rose to become the youngest Cavalry Captain in their history. After his father's death, Inspector Eroch ordered him to "conceal the truth" and present it as an accident to protect the Knights' reputation. Diluc did not even argue. He resigned that day and left his Vision behind. Within the four years he was away, Eroch was exposed as a traitor and purged. Diluc still criticises the Knights as slow and inefficient, but he respects individuals.

Eroch had been Varka's trusted deputy. Jealous of Varka, he was drawn into treason by Dottore, maintained Ursa's seal and broke it. When Varka finally cornered him, Eroch took his own life, laughing. In 6.6 the elderly knight Adorno added that Ursa's defeat by "a mere merchant" spoiled Eroch's plan to seize power through fear, so he suppressed it. Diluc's reply to the regret of the old knights is brief: "...But they weren't there, were they?"

5.comment: Diluc: Northern Intelligence Network and Nefer
5.content:
While hunting the Fatui, Diluc drew the Harbingers' attention and barely escaped death. He was saved by an observer from a vast underground intelligence network in the north, who had been watching him and approved of his methods. He joined and rose into its upper ranks. Its members are volunteers who often give up their status and even their names. The network is run by Nefer from the Curatorium of Secrets in Nod-Krai. She calls him "Owl", names him a key Mondstadt informant, and says working with him is a pleasure because "he pays promptly".

In 6.3, when Varka guessed Nefer had heard about the Knights' customs from "Diluc", she hushed him: "We don't use people's real names at work." Nefer describes their collaboration as long-standing and too valuable to risk.

6.content: Diluc's hunt taught him that the Fatui make counterfeit Visions called Delusions, which amplify the user's power to the extreme at the risk of backfiring, as one did on his father. He laid waste to many Fatui strongholds. In the Prologue he interrogated Fatui agents and raided their hideout to recover the Holy Lyre. The wiki says he also bought up vials claimed to hold the Anemo Archon's breath to keep them from the Fatui. He holds that to the lost a Vision is a light from the gods, and to those with conviction it is "little more than badges of conviction".

7.content: Prologue, 1.0. The Traveler first saw Diluc at the Temple of the Wolf, where he killed a Hydro Abyss Mage and called the Knights inefficient. When the Knights chased Venti and the Traveler for the stolen Holy Lyre, Diluc hid them upstairs in Angel's Share and misdirected the guards. Venti then explained the situation in song. Diluc worked his contacts, briefed Jean, tracked the Fatui to a stronghold outside the city and recovered the Lyre with the Traveler. He vetoed summoning Dvalin at the winery because he did not want to rebuild it, and agreed to Starsnatch Cliff. When the Abyss Order turned Dvalin away and Venti was revealed as Barbatos, Diluc showed no surprise and pointed the group at the Abyss Order. He joined the push into Stormterror's Lair.

8.comment: Diluc: Ursa the Drake and A Knight's Legacy
8.content: In Lohen's story quest (6.6), strange monsters gathered around Dornman Port, where Dawn Winery caravans pass. Diluc investigated in person. He met Adorno, the Traveler and Lohen at a scene wiped "clean", suspected someone with advance intel was eliminating the monsters, and later caught Lohen at it. The monsters bore Ursa's Flesh. Varka explained that Eroch and one of Dottore's Segments had extracted a serum from the drake, and Diluc concluded someone had restarted the experiments. He warned that "wealth, power, authority" can turn good people into villains. With Varka and the Traveler he tracked Lohen to Eroch's hidden laboratory. There the trainee medic Theodore had been using the serum to prolong Adorno's life. Together they fought Ursa's remnants and destroyed the flesh. Adorno died soon after.

key: To Those Who Embark on the Expedition
9.content: Varka is the Grand Master, his father's old friend. Varka says the wind of Mondstadt is free to come and go, so Diluc may stay away, and Varka is equally free to keep pestering him, though he fears being blacklisted by the Dawn Winery. Before the expedition Varka cornered him for a drink, apologised and asked him to rejoin. In 6.4 the Traveler delivered a letter from Nod-Krai renewing the condolences and the invitation. Diluc admitted he "wasn't seeing the full picture" back then and has reflected, but refused again: the Knights' leaders are too upright to see the shadows beneath so large an organisation. Rosaria believes Varka keeps asking to tell Diluc he is not alone, mindful of a righteous knight who was once driven to extremes.

10.content: Jean calls Diluc her senior and says she has the utmost respect for him. She accepts that he has reasons to criticise the Knights and hopes to earn his good opinion by her work. He says trivial matters are her greatest enemy and that her unparalleled sense of responsibility keeps her from finding her true calling. In the Prologue he briefed her on the Lyre theft. In Jean's Story Quest he lent Angel's Share for her party, not to sponsor the Knights but in appreciation of her hard work.

11.content: Venti haunts Angel's Share for free drinks, and Diluc is not inclined to provide them. During the Stormterror crisis he hid Venti in the tavern, heard the story as a song and helped. When Dvalin named Venti as Barbatos, Diluc was unsurprised, and he keeps the secret. In Venti's Story Quest, Diluc deadpanned that he had no imaginary friends, not even fifteen years ago.
